newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-The sky or intervention the limit for dlr.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-The sky or intervention the limit for dlr.

text.p: The dollar is likely to keep on packing momentum to attack new resistance levels against key currencies unless central banks' intervention gets in the way, technical analysts said on Monday.

The dollar set a new 1997 high -- also a fresh three-year high -- against the German mark at 1.7389 as finance ministers of the Group of Seven failed to convince the foreign exchange market during their weekend meeting that they really mean to end the bull run, they added.
"The dollar bulls are out and what else is there to say," noted Ben Morden, technical analyst at I.D.E.A.
"It's good that we held above 1.7250-mark support," Morden said. "Maybe, we could make a quick move through 1.74 marks and target 1.7500/10, a retracement level."
Morden added that a run all the way to the February 8, 1994, high of 1.7686 could not be ruled out either.
MCM CurrencyWatch technical analysts agreed daily studies are "positive" for dollar-mark and that "further strength toward 1.7535/1.7680 is possible in coming sessions."
They said only the loss of 1.7220/25-mark area would point to renewed selling pressure with a deeper downside to 1.7175 to 1.7135 marks.
But Morden noted dollar/mark is not giving any sign of weakness as it closed on Monday above 1.73 marks for the first time in more than three years.
The dollar last visited these levels in February 1994 as the Federal Reserve kicked off a rapid-fire tightening cycle that weighed on U.S. financial assets, mainly in fixed income.
At 127.08, dollar/yen came close on Monday to revisiting its 1997 high of 127.19 set on April 10, Morden added.
"We can revisit that 127.19-yen level near-term. Going to 127.75 yen is a minor objective, and 128.90 is the real objective," the I.D.E.A. analyst stated.
However, fears of intervention by at least one Group of Three central banks remained the wild card, analysts said.
But they agreed that dollar/yen would have to break strong support at 126.30/35 to reopen the downside while 128.20 was a first important line of resistance.
Morden also noted "dollar/Swiss is strong but does not have the same kind of aggressiveness because mark/Swiss has been weighing on it. Cable is pretty flat."
At the close in New York, the dollar was quoted at 1.7320/30 marks vs 1.7316/19 at the open, and at 123.83/88 vs 126.63. ((-- Isabelle Clary, 212-859-1666))
